references.text: Esther's involuntary identification with her people's fate parallels Joseph's brothers' inability to see their father's grief without the lost son.
Jacob's fear in 42:38 is the direct cause of Judah's dilemma and pledge in 44:34; both concern the father's death through the loss of his last son.
The verses are part of the same dialogue sequence; 44:26 sets the condition that Judah commits to fulfilling in 44:34 for his father's sake.
44:22 is the general warning that Judah makes his own personal concern and pledge to protect in 44:34.
Judah's fear in 44:34 is a direct response to Jacob's reaction in 37:35; he wants to prevent his father from weeping himself down into the realm of the dead again.
43:5 sets the condition that Judah guarantees will be fulfilled in 44:34; both concern the necessary presence of the youngest son.
